_note: Swift/SwiftUI design-slop rule file. Mirrors the web detector-rules.json shape (id/severity/source_rant + machine-readable finding schema {antipattern,name,description,file,line,snippet}) but the rules are evaluated by an in-process SwiftSyntax AST walk in mcp/swift-design-detector (NOT by regex on CSS). source_rant paths point under docs/concepts/ios-design-contract/rants/ which Pass 2 of requirement ios-impeccable-adaptation will author; until then they are forward references and are documented here as the rule's provenance. scope_in_token_dirs is the keystone correctness flag (see detector-config-schema.md): when false, the rule is SUPPRESSED for files matching a configured token-dir glob (defining the literal there IS the token layer's job); when true, the rule STILL FIRES inside token dirs because that is precisely where hue-coded / off-palette / Tailwind-palette / gradient slop lives.

finding_schema.antipattern: stable rule id (matches a rule.id below)
finding_schema.name: human-readable rule name
finding_schema.description: what is wrong + the corrective move
finding_schema.file: absolute path of the scanned file
finding_schema.line: 1-based source line of the offending node

rules.name: Off-palette hue
rules.description: A chromatic color hex was introduced whose hue is not blue/neutral. The PeptideFox v7 law (peptidefox-ios .claude/CLAUDE.md §6.1) is a blue-only accent palette over neutrals; orange (Metabolic), teal (Healing), pink (GLOW), purple/violet (NAD/KLOW), and lavender are off-palette. Remove the hue or re-derive it from the blue accent. STILL fires inside token dirs because the off-palette slop is defined in the token file itself.

detector._note: A hex is clean if it is near-neutral (channel spread < neutral_chroma_max) OR its HSL hue falls inside an allowed (blue) range. Anything chromatic outside the blue band is off-palette. Blue band 205-245deg covers #336CFF (~223) and #2563eb (~221) while excluding teal (~173), green (~145), orange (~25), pink (~330), purple (~271), and the lavender tint #EDE8FF (~253). neutral_chroma_max=16 keeps the v7 neutral/ink/cool-grey text ramp clean (max legit non-blue-band chroma is v7SoftDark/v7TextSoftDark at 14) while exposing the lavender haze tint (#EDE8FF, chroma 23) and the deprecated purple tints (#f3e8ff, chroma 23) as off-palette. The cool-grey text tokens with chroma >16 (#7F86A0 c33, #586070 c24) stay clean because their hue (~220-227) is inside the blue band. Verified zero false positives across every hex-defined v7 token in PeptideFox ColorTokens.swift.

rules.name: Raw hex literal outside the token layer
rules.description: A raw color hex literal (Color(hex:"#...") or UIColor literal) appears in a view/feature file instead of referencing a named design token. Color authority belongs to the token layer; views must consume tokens. SUPPRESSED inside token dirs — defining hex literals IS the token layer's job.

detector._note: Flags any 6- or 3-digit hex string passed to a Color(hex:)/UIColor initializer. Suppressed in token dirs so the token file can legally define literals; off-palette-hue still polices WHICH literals are allowed there.

rules.name: Hue-coded category
rules.description: A categorical concept (compound type, metabolic vs healing, per-peptide accent) is encoded by assigning each category its own hue. Categories must be distinguished by typography/layout/iconography, not a rainbow. Collapse per-category colors to the single blue accent + neutrals. STILL fires inside token dirs because the per-category color map (e.g. CompoundColorScheme.forCompound switching primary color by case, *Accent token families) lives in the token file.

detector._note: Fires when (a) a switch/case maps category cases to differing color values, or (b) a family of >= min_distinct_category_tokens tokens named <category>Accent assigns chromatic, differing hues per category.

rules.name: Tailwind palette hex
rules.description: A hex value copied verbatim from the Tailwind default palette (the canonical AI-slop fingerprint). These are not brand colors; they are the default every generator emits. Replace with brand tokens. STILL fires inside token dirs — the Tailwind hexes were pasted directly into the token definitions.

detector._note: Case-insensitive match on the hex digits (with or without leading #). Deliberately EXCLUDES the legitimate blue tokens #336CFF and #2563eb. Note 3b82f6/60a5fa/6366f1 are blue-family Tailwind values; they are flagged as tailwind-palette-hex (copied-from-Tailwind smell) even though off-palette-hue would pass them — the two P0 rules are independent and either firing blocks.

rules.name: Gradient fill
rules.description: A LinearGradient/RadialGradient/AngularGradient (or .fill(.linearGradient...)) is used as a surface/text fill. Gradients read as decorative AI slop; use a solid token. STILL fires inside token dirs because gradient stop tokens (gradientStart/gradientEnd) and gradient definitions are declared there.

detector._note: Fires on a Gradient initializer/member-call expression, OR on a token declaration whose name contains 'gradient' (case-insensitive) so gradientStart/gradientEnd are caught at the source.

rules.name: Display font below size floor
rules.description: A display/hero typeface (Brown LL Inline / heroInline) is instantiated below its size floor. TypographyTokens.swift documents display roles at 28-80pt and asserts Inline MUST be >= 28pt ('Inline collapses below this size'). The detector floor sits at 24pt — below the 28pt display floor but above the 16pt body ceiling — so it catches genuinely-too-small display type without flagging body/label sizes. STILL fires inside token dirs because the display tokens are declared there.

detector._note: Derived from TypographyTokens.swift: display roles run 28-80pt (Display.small=28 is the smallest display role; heroInline asserts >=28). Floor set to 24 (below the 28 display floor, above the 16 Body.large ceiling). Fires when a heroInline(...) / BrownLLInline-based Font.custom is created with size < floor_pt.

rules.name: System-font reflex
rules.description: Reflexively reaching for .system(...)/Font.system or a bare .font(.title)/.headline system text style instead of the bundled brand family (Brown LL via Font.primary). Advisory: the brand has a real typeface; use it. SUPPRESSED inside token dirs because the token factories may legitimately compose relativeTo: system text styles.

detector._note: Fires on Font.system(...) / .system(size:...) usages in non-token files. Does not flag the relativeTo: TextStyle argument used by the brand factories.

rules.name: Magic-number spacing
rules.description: A raw numeric literal is passed to .padding(...), spacing:, VStack/HStack(spacing:), .frame insets, etc. instead of a Spacing token. Advisory: route spacing through the scale for rhythm. SUPPRESSED inside token dirs because the Spacing scale itself is defined with numeric literals there.

detector._note: Fires on integer/float literals supplied to padding()/spacing: arguments in non-token files. 0 is ignored (zero-out is intentional).

rules.name: Shadow reflex
rules.description: Reflexive .shadow(...) (especially colored or large-radius) to fake depth/glow — the dark-glow tell ported to SwiftUI. Advisory: prefer a hairline/material or a token-defined elevation. Fires in token dirs too because elevation/shadow tokens can encode the reflex.

detector._note: Fires on .shadow(...) modifier calls. Colored/large-radius shadows are the worst case; v1 flags any explicit .shadow as advisory.

rules.name: Spring overshoot
rules.description: An over-bouncy spring animation (interpolatingSpring / .spring with high bounce / low damping) — the bounce-easing tell. Advisory: real objects decelerate smoothly; reduce bounce / raise damping. SUPPRESSED inside token dirs (animation tokens may legitimately tune curves centrally).

detector._note: Fires on .spring/interpolatingSpring calls whose bounce > bounce_max or dampingFraction < damping_min. A bare .spring() with no tuning is advisory-flagged only when other overshoot signals are absent (v1: flag explicit over-bounce).

rules.name: Monospace fatigue
rules.description: Over-reaching for the mono/accent family (Brown Mono LL / accentMono / .monospaced) beyond its sanctioned use (micro nav labels, technical identifiers) — e.g. mono on body or numeric data. Advisory: reserve mono for micro labels. SUPPRESSED inside token dirs because the mono factory + sanctioned mono tokens are declared there.

detector._note: Fires on accentMono(...)/.monospaced()/.monospacedDigit() usages in non-token files. Advisory only.

rules.name: iOS default reflex
rules.description: Shipping the platform default where the brand demands a considered, custom treatment — the iOS analogue of the web generic-default attractor. Three shapes: (a) a native control init (Menu/Picker) standing in for a custom control, (b) a default-chrome modifier (.contextMenu), or (c) the accent reflex .tint(.blue) reaching for the stock system accent instead of the brand accent token. Replace with the bundled custom control / brand accent. SUPPRESSED inside token dirs (the token layer may legitimately reference system controls/colors when defining adaptions). Owner can sanction a specific use via .design-overrides.json (design-overrides-schema.md).

detector._note: Data-driven match lists so the owner tunes without recompiling. Fires on a FunctionCallExprSyntax whose callee name is a native_control_types init, OR a default_chrome_modifiers modifier, OR an accent_reflex_calls call (tint) whose first argument is a base-less member access (.blue) in accent_reflex_values. The accent case deliberately requires the member-access form so .tint(BrandColor.accent) / .tint(Color.brandAccent) pass clean.
